correctness.rationale: The chordal graph indicator is defined for every labelled simple graph over 2^(n choose 2) edge bits, with unnormalized Walsh sum. Exhaustive five-vertex enumeration of all 1024 graph masks gives 822 chordal graphs; 34 vertex-permutation frequency orbits include exactly three zero Walsh classes (representatives 28,31,185, sizes 30,30,60), total 120 zeros and rank 904. In six vertices 18154 chordal graphs with 8524 containing any specified edge; product expansion (-1)^{sum bits}=product(1-2x_e) gives W_6(S)=18154-2(8524)|S|=2 mod 4 for every frequency, and one witness S with mask 639 gives W_6=2, hence full rank and sharp inverse norm 1/2. Inspected two independent exact chordality recognizers (induced-cycle forbidden patterns and perfect elimination) and fast Walsh transform logic; independently enumerated all masks with an original PEO/Walsh implementation, reproducing 822,18154,120,0, witness 2, min magnitude 2 and Parseval.
residual_risks: Only vertex orders five and six treated; the six-vertex congruence is not asserted for all n.

value.rationale: The class of labeled chordal graphs is mathematically natural via perfect elimination/chordless-cycle properties. Complete five-vertex cancellation geometry and abrupt restoration of full invertibility at six vertices answer a meaningful exact spectral question about convolution on the complete edge cube; the sharp inverse gap and three graph motifs are neither mere unsigned table recitation nor a random arbitrary mask slice.
residual_risks: Finite at n=5,6 only; no claim for all orders or asymptotic behavior.

limitations: Wormald 1985 full text not directly inspected; bounded best-of-knowledge novelty.
